scenarioName: Dehydration — Difficult IV Access in a Fragile Nursing Home Resident

scenarioStory.history: Nursing home staff report the patient has eaten and drunk very little over the past three days, becoming progressively weaker and less interactive. No fever reported by staff. He is oriented to person only at baseline per staff, unchanged today.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew finds a frail 71-year-old male in bed, arousable but slow to respond, with dry mucous membranes and tenting skin consistent with volume depletion after several days of poor intake. → IV access obtained within two attempts: Crew successfully cannulates a peripheral vein despite the patient's thin, fragile veins, checks blood glucose, and initiates an isotonic fluid bolus. → Fluid bolus given and improving: Patient's perfusion improves following isotonic fluid resuscitation. Crew continues reassessment en route to the hospital.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Poor oral intake and weakness for three days

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew finds a frail 71-year-old male in bed, arousable but slow to respond, with dry mucous membranes and tenting skin consistent with volume depletion after several days of poor intake.

scenarioEvents.name: IV access obtained within two attempts
scenarioEvents.description: Crew successfully cannulates a peripheral vein despite the patient's thin, fragile veins, checks blood glucose, and initiates an isotonic fluid bolus.
relatedChecklist: Recognize hypovolemia from dry mucous membranes, tenting skin, tachycardia, borderline BP
Check blood glucose to rule out hypoglycemia as a contributing cause
Establish peripheral IV access, using a proximal/larger vein given fragile skin and small distal veins
Administer 500 mL NS bolus IV, pressure-infused over less than 15 minutes, reassess

scenarioEvents.name: Fluid bolus given and improving
scenarioEvents.description: Patient's perfusion improves following isotonic fluid resuscitation. Crew continues reassessment en route to the hospital.
relatedChecklist: Reassess vital signs and mental status; continue fluids toward MAP goal of 65 mmHg
Provide advance notification to the receiving hospital

scenarioEvents.name: IV access fails twice / exceeds 90 seconds
scenarioEvents.description: Peripheral IV attempts fail on the patient's thin, fragile, rolling veins. Per protocol, the crew transitions to IO access to avoid further delay in fluid resuscitation.
relatedChecklist: Place IO needle after two failed IV attempts / 90 seconds elapsed
Administer 500 mL NS bolus via IO, pressure-infused, reassess
